title: Escape the Failing Startup
description: Your tech startup is in freefall -- servers are crashing, finances are bleeding cash, and investors are about to pull out. Race through three high-pressure rooms: debug a critical memory leak in the Server Room, slash expenses strategically in the Finance Office, and deliver a data-driven pitch in the Boardroom. Solve real-world business puzzles under a 5-minute countdown to rescue your company from the brink of failure!
learning_objectives: Diagnose and fix common software engineering problems such as memory leaks by reading error logs and understanding code behavior
Analyze financial statements including burn rate, revenue, and runway to make strategic cost-cutting decisions that preserve core operations
Evaluate vendor contracts and identify opportunities to reduce expenses without sacrificing business quality
Craft a compelling investor pitch using growth metrics, retention data, unit economics, and competitive positioning
Practice time-pressured decision-making that mirrors the urgency founders face when their startup is in crisis

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: Explore each room by tapping on clues -- error logs, spreadsheets, and sticky notes
Read each clue carefully to gather information needed to solve the room's puzzle
Answer the puzzle question correctly to unlock the next room
Progress through the Server Room, Finance Office, and CEO's Office to save the startup
Solve all puzzles before the 5-minute timer expires to escape!
tips: Some clues unlock other clues -- examine everything in order to reveal all the information
Sticky notes and whiteboard messages often contain passwords or key details for later rooms
Think like a real startup founder -- focus on fixing the root cause, not applying band-aids

rooms.title: The Server Room
rooms.description: Alarms are blaring! The company servers are crashing and customer data is at risk. You need to find the source of the problem.

clues.label: Error Log
clues.content: The error log reads: 'FATAL: Memory leak detected in auth.js at line 42. Cache array growing unbounded. System memory at 98%.'
clues.hint: The error mentions a specific file and line number. What happens when arrays grow forever?

clues.label: Whiteboard Code
clues.content: Someone wrote on the whiteboard: 'var cache = []; function processRequest() { cache.push(data); /* TODO: clear old entries */ }'

clues.label: Sticky Note
clues.content: A sticky note on the monitor says: 'Remember! The backup password is the year we founded the company: 2019'
clues.hint: This might come in handy later...

puzzles.question: How do you fix the server memory leak?
options: Buy a server with more RAM
Restart the server every hour with a cron job
puzzles.explanation: Clearing the cache array after each batch prevents unbounded memory growth. The other options are band-aids, not real fixes!

rooms.title: The Finance Office
rooms.description: The servers are stabilized! But now you discover the company finances are a mess. Investors are threatening to pull out tomorrow.

clues.label: Financial Spreadsheet
clues.content: The spreadsheet shows: Revenue ₹5L/month, Expenses ₹8L/month. Burn rate: ₹3L/month. Runway: 2 months left.
clues.hint: You need to either increase revenue or cut expenses.

clues.label: Investor Email
clues.content: Email from investor: 'We need to see a path to profitability. If you can show 40% cost reduction while maintaining growth, we'll double down.'

clues.label: Vendor Contracts
clues.content: Three vendor contracts found: Cloud hosting ₹2L/mo (can switch to cheaper provider for ₹80K), Premium tools ₹1.5L/mo (free alternatives exist for 80% of features), Office rent ₹1.5L/mo (can go remote).

puzzles.question: Which combination cuts costs by at least 40% (₹3.2L) while maintaining operations?
options: Switch cloud provider (save ₹1.2L) + Go remote (save ₹1.5L) + Free tools (save ₹1.5L) = ₹4.2L saved
Fire half the team to save ₹4L immediately
Take a personal loan to cover expenses for 6 months
Switch to cloud only (save ₹1.2L) — small steps first
puzzles.explanation: Strategic cost cutting across vendors, office, and tools saves ₹4.2L (52.5%) without losing team members or taking risky loans. This shows the investor a clear path to profitability!

rooms.title: The Boardroom
rooms.description: Final challenge! The investor is on a video call. You have one chance to deliver the perfect pitch to save the company.

clues.label: Growth Metrics
clues.content: Dashboard shows: 15,000 active users (up 200% in 3 months), 4.5-star app rating, 68% monthly retention rate. Customer acquisition cost: ₹150.
clues.hint: These numbers tell a story. Which metrics would impress an investor?

clues.label: Competitor Analysis
clues.content: Closest competitor charges ₹500/user/month with only 3.2-star rating. Your free tier converts 12% to paid at ₹200/user/month.

clues.label: Customer Testimonial
clues.content: 'This app changed how our school teaches financial literacy. Students are actually excited to learn!' — Principal, Delhi Public School

puzzles.question: Which pitch opening would be most effective for the investor?
options: We have 15K users growing 200% quarterly with 68% retention — better metrics than our competitor at half the price. With our cost restructuring, we reach profitability in 4 months.
Our app is really cool and students love it. We just need more money to keep going.
If you don't invest, we'll go bankrupt in 2 months and 15,000 students will lose access.
We're the best edtech startup in India and we deserve ₹10 crore valuation.
puzzles.explanation: Leading with data (growth, retention, unit economics) and showing a clear path to profitability is what investors want to hear. The other options rely on emotion, threats, or ego — none of which build investor confidence.

transfer_exercises.real_world: Making fast calls during a team project deadline crunch
transfer_exercises.challenge: Practice making a decision in under 60 seconds on something you've been procrastinating. Reflect on the outcome.

transfer_exercises.game_context: Recovering from mistakes in rapid gameplay
transfer_exercises.real_world: Bouncing back after a failed presentation or test
transfer_exercises.challenge: Write down one recent failure and three specific things you learned from it.

glossary_terms.definition: The mental effort required to process information and make decisions.
glossary_terms.example: Having too many options at once makes decisions harder and slower.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Working memory has limits. Experts chunk information into patterns, reducing cognitive load and enabling faster decisions.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Experienced doctors diagnose faster not because they think harder, but because they recognize patterns instantly.

glossary_terms.definition: Identifying recurring structures or relationships in information.
glossary_terms.example: Noticing that certain question types always have two plausible answers helps you focus faster.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Pattern recognition is a core skill in chess, medicine, engineering, and sport. It develops through deliberate practice.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Air traffic controllers recognize dangerous flight patterns faster than computers because of years of pattern training.

glossary_terms.definition: The ability to direct mental attention toward what matters most and ignore distractions.
glossary_terms.example: Under time pressure, completing questions you're confident about before tackling harder ones.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Focus is a trainable skill. The Pomodoro method, mindfulness, and deliberate practice all improve sustained attention.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Olympic athletes train mental focus as rigorously as physical skills — pressure performance depends on it.

coaching_moment: If you get something wrong, reset and continue. Resilience isn't about never failing — it's about how quickly you get back on track.
cultural_context: India's startup ecosystem — the world's third largest — has produced over 100 unicorns. Escape the Failing Startup develops the entrepreneurial thinking that is reshaping India's economy and creating new career pathways for young Indians.
reflection_prompt: What pattern did you start to recognize as you played? How will you use it next time?
